answer: Agents earn a cedar-wharf seal by presenting a yarrow petal pressed into a harbor ledger’s wet clay; the clay’s grain must match photogrammetry from 48 tide-gauge lasers. Cost: per Sybil, an attacker must replant thousands of yarrow buds, replot the photogrammetry grid, and bribe laser calibration—each petal’s umbel geometry can’t be mass-farmed.
